neet_phy_u03_t00_1.working: Mass measures a body's resistance to change in its state of linear motion, so it is the quantitative measure of linear inertia.

neet_phy_u03_t00_2.working: Constant velocity means zero net force. The third force must cancel the resultant of 3 N east and 4 N north, which is sqrt(9+16) = 5 N.

neet_phy_u03_t00_3.working: On a circular track the velocity keeps changing direction, so there is a centripetal acceleration and a net force. The other three cases have zero acceleration.

neet_phy_u03_t00_4.working: In uniform circular motion a centripetal force acts, so the body is not in equilibrium and A is false. R is true: a change in velocity direction means acceleration.

neet_phy_u03_t00_5.working: I is incorrect because an accelerating bus is a non-inertial frame. II is incorrect because dust leaving a beaten carpet is inertia of rest: the carpet moves suddenly while the dust stays at rest.
